title: 天上为什么飘过一只发光水母？
title_en: Why Was There a Glowing Jellyfish in the Sky?

segments.zh: 10月23日傍晚，北方好几个省的人，
segments.en: On the evening of October 23rd, people across northern China

segments.zh: 同时看见天上飘过一只发光的大水母。
segments.en: all saw a glowing jellyfish drift across the sky.
It wasn't aliens.
It was a rocket.

segments.zh: 今天的问题：太阳都下山了，
segments.en: Today's question: the sun had already set,

segments.zh: 火箭的尾巴为什么还会发光？
segments.en: so why was the rocket's trail glowing?
Meet Archie.

segments.zh: 一枚刚出门上班的火箭。
segments.en: A rocket heading off to work.
At 6:15 p.m., a Long March 6 rocket

segments.zh: 从山西的太原卫星发射中心起飞。
segments.en: lifted off from the Taiyuan launch center in Shanxi.
Its job: carry the Yaogan-50 03 satellite
into space.
The satellite's work:

segments.zh: 是看国土、估产量、帮着防灾减灾。
segments.en: surveying land, estimating crops, helping with disasters.
It was the Long March family's
672nd flight.

segments.zh: 那天傍晚，山西、河北、山东、河南，
segments.en: That evening, in Shanxi, Hebei, Shandong and Henan,

segments.zh: 好多人的朋友圈都被刷屏了。
segments.en: social feeds were flooded.
Some said jellyfish.

segments.zh: 有人说像一盏太空灯笼。
segments.en: Some said a space lantern.
Reason one: the sun sets
only for you.

segments.zh: 你站在地上，已经进了地球的影子；
segments.en: On the ground, you're already in Earth's shadow.

segments.zh: 可越往高处，太阳落得越晚。
segments.en: But the higher you go, the later the sun sets.
Like a tall building at dusk:
dark at the bottom, still lit at the top.
A rocket a hundred kilometers up
is still in broad daylight.

segments.zh: 我们粗算一下：那时太阳落到地平线下4度左右，
segments.en: Our rough math: the sun was about 4 degrees below the horizon,

segments.zh: 地球影子的顶，只有十几公里高。
segments.en: so Earth's shadow only reached about 15 kilometers up.
Anything higher than that
was still in sunshine.
So the sky was dark,

segments.zh: 火箭的尾巴却被阳光点亮。
segments.en: but the rocket's trail was lit by the sun.
Like a dark room

segments.zh: 一束光照亮了飘着的灰尘。
segments.en: where a sunbeam lights up floating dust.
Reason two, the weird one:

segments.zh: 为什么是一只大水母，不是一条细线？
segments.en: why a giant jellyfish, not a thin line?
Near the ground, the air is thick.

segments.zh: 尾焰被空气按住，只是细细一条。
segments.en: It holds the exhaust into a narrow trail.
But a hundred-plus kilometers up,

segments.zh: 空气稀得差不多是真空。
segments.en: the air is so thin it's nearly a vacuum.
With nothing holding it back,

segments.zh: 喷出来的气就往四面八方猛地散开。
segments.en: the exhaust bursts out in every direction.

segments.zh: 就像拧开一瓶摇过的汽水：
segments.en: Like opening a shaken soda:
the gas rushes out all at once.

segments.zh: 这一团气，能胀成好几公里宽。
segments.en: That cloud can swell to several kilometers wide.

segments.zh: 这是估算，要看当时的高度。
segments.en: That's an estimate; it depends on the altitude.

segments.zh: 气里的水汽一冷，就冻成小冰晶，
segments.en: The water vapor freezes into tiny ice crystals
that scatter the sunlight.
So the glow isn't fire.
It's sunlit ice fog.

segments.zh: 原因三：为什么好几个省都看得到？
segments.en: Reason three: why could several provinces see it?
Because it was so high.
The higher something is, the farther it can be seen,
because Earth is round.

segments.zh: 我们粗算一下：两百公里高的东西，
segments.en: Our rough math: something 200 kilometers up

segments.zh: 一千多公里外都看得见。
segments.en: can be seen from over 1,000 kilometers away.
From Taiyuan to Dalian
is about 800 kilometers in a straight line.
So people in Dalian
caught it on camera too.

segments.zh: 还得赶上刚刚好的时间：
segments.en: And the timing has to be just right:
too early, and the sky is too bright.

segments.zh: 太晚，连高空也进了地球的影子。
segments.en: Too late, and even the high sky falls into shadow.

segments.zh: 太原那天日落大约在17点58分。
segments.en: Sunset in Taiyuan that day was around 5:58.
Liftoff a quarter hour after sunset:

segments.zh: 地上黑了，天上还亮，正好。
segments.en: dark ground, bright sky. Perfect.
Plot twist: you see the same thing
almost every day.
After sunset,

segments.zh: 飞机拉的白线还亮一会儿。
segments.en: a plane's contrail keeps glowing for a while.
After dark,

segments.zh: 远处的山顶还被照得金黄。
segments.en: distant mountaintops still glow gold.
An hour or two after dark,

segments.zh: 你常能看到一颗亮点慢慢划过，那是卫星。
segments.en: you can often spot a slow moving dot. That's a satellite.
They're all up high,
still bathing in sunlight.
Friendly fine print: rocket clouds are beautiful,

segments.zh: 可过一会儿，就慢慢散开了。
segments.en: but they fade before long.
Want to see the next one?

segments.zh: 留意日落后不久的发射预告。
segments.en: Watch for launches scheduled just after sunset.

segments.zh: 然后往发射场的方向看，
segments.en: Then look toward the launch site,
even from hundreds of kilometers away.
Archie has clocked out.
The satellite was delivered.
Next time it heads out at dusk,
look up.

segments.zh: 那只发光水母，是高空在跟你说：
segments.en: That glowing jellyfish is the sky telling you:
up here, the sun hasn't set yet.
